name: All for One and One for All Poker

overview.description: All for One and One for All is a high-churn variant of Five-Card Draw. Unlike standard poker where you draw once, here players can repeatedly exchange their entire hand or a single card through multiple rounds of betting until the deck is nearly exhausted.
overview.originName: All for One and One for All Poker

history.origins: A relatively modern home-game variant of Five-Card Draw. Its name is a playful reference to the Three Musketeers, echoing the 'One card or All cards' binary choice of the discard phase.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Appears in American 'dealer's choice' home games.
1990s-2000s: Described in printed home-game rules and early online poker variant archives.
history.evolution: Evolved from standard Draw Poker by removing the one-draw limit, turning the game into one of attrition and probability tracking.
history.cultural: Popular in low-stakes social poker nights where 'active' games with lots of betting rounds are preferred.

setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards face-down. Antes are placed.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best 5-card poker hand at showdown or by forcing all other players to fold.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Initial Deal**: 5 cards each. Initial betting round. 2. **Repeated Draw Phases**: Each active player must choose one of three options: 
   - **All for One**: Discard your entire 5-card hand and draw 5 new ones.
   - **One for All**: Discard exactly 1 card and draw 1 new one.
   - **Stand Pat**: Keep your current hand (once you stand pat, you cannot draw in future rounds).
3. **Betting**: Each draw phase is followed by a full betting round. 4. **Repetition**: Draw and betting rounds continue until the deck has too few cards left to fulfill a worst-case draw scenario (i.e., every participant drawing 5). 5. **Showdown**: Remaining players reveal hands. Best hand according to standard rankings wins.
keyRules: No half-measures: You cannot discard 2, 3, or 4 cards. It is strictly 1 or 5 or 0.
Standing Pat: Once a player stands pat, they are locked into that hand for the remainder of the deal.
End Condition: The game ends automatically when the deck contains fewer than (Active Players * 5) cards, or by mutual agreement if betting becomes circular.

strategy.basic: If you don't have at least a pair, go 'All for One'. If you have a potential flush/straight draw, go 'One for All'.
strategy.intermediate: Bluffing: Standing pat early can scare opponents into thinking you have a made hand, even if you are holding junk. However, they have many rounds to figure you out.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting: Because so many cards are being cycled (draw 5, draw 5...), you can track which cards are unlikely to appear in and your opponents' hands. If many Spades have been discarded, your flush draw is dead.
tips: The deck disappears fast. If 6 people are playing and 4 draw 'All for One', the deck is half gone in one round.
Don't be afraid to 'All for One' twice in a row if your first exchange is also rubbish.

list.name: Musketeer Wilds
list.description: Deuces/Jacks are wild to increase the power level of the multiple draws.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation adjusts wild cards only; engine-level parameter overrides for wilds are not yet modeled.

difficulty.easy: Almost always chooses 'All for One' unless they hand a pair. Never stands pat as a bluff.
difficulty.medium: Calculates the probability of completing a straight/flush with a 'One for All' draw. Folds to high bets early.
difficulty.hard: Tracks discarded cards to adjust draw probabilities. Uses 'Stand Pat' strategically on the 2nd round to force folds.

phases.label: Antes
phases.notes: Each player contributes ante before cards are dealt.

phases.label: Initial Deal
phases.notes: Deal five face-down cards to each player.

phases.label: All / One / Stand Pat
phases.notes: Each active player may stand pat, exchange one, or exchange all five with stock-safety restriction.

phases.label: Betting After Draw
phases.notes: Repeat draw then betting until stock is too short for another draw cycle.

phases.label: Showdown
phases.notes: Remaining active players reveal; standard poker hand ranking applies.

phases.label: Award Pot
phases.notes: Award the pot to last active player or best showdown hand.

ante.description: Post mandatory ante before the hand.
ante.constraints: Required once per hand before dealing.

deal.description: Dealer gives five down cards to each player.

reveal_market.reason: Five-card draw with one shared buy; no market reveal phase.

buy_market.reason: Draw is from stock; one card bought from central pool in draw round, not market.

buy_stock.reason: Drawing is replacement from stock (1 or 5 cards); no separate stock purchase.

fold.description: Fold and surrender claim to this pot.

check.description: Check when no wager is owed.
check.constraints: Available only when action is unopened.

call.constraints: Only when there is an open wager.

bet.description: Open wagering in a betting round.
bet.constraints: Only when no bet has been placed yet.

raise.constraints: Only when a bet or raise is already open.

declare.reason: Winner determined at showdown; no separate declare phase.

award_pot.description: Award pot to surviving player or best showdown hand.
award_pot.constraints: System action after fold-out or showdown.

play_card.reason: Play is draw-and-discard (1 or 5 cards) then showdown; no single play_card to table.

draw.description: Draw replacement cards from stock after chosen discard count.
draw.constraints: During draw rounds only; replacements must equal discards.

discard.description: Discard either one card or all five cards.
discard.constraints: Only counts 1 or 5 are allowed; 5-card exchange blocked if it would starve remaining players of one-card draws.

pass.description: Stand pat and draw zero cards.

bid.reason: Fixed-limit betting rounds only; no bidding.

meld.reason: Standard five-card draw poker; no melds.

go_out.reason: Hand ends at showdown; no go-out declaration.

drawSources.notes: Draw count equals chosen discard count (0, 1, or 5 choices expressed by pass/discard).

notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Standard 52-card deck; no special action or bonus cards.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Draw poker; aim is best five-card hand at showdown, not emptying the hand.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: No capture-from-table mechanic; draw and betting only.

edgeCases.text: A 5-card exchange is illegal if it would leave too few stock cards for each remaining active player to exchange at least one card in that same draw round.
After a betting round, if stock has fewer cards than active players, skip further drawing and go directly to showdown.
Successive draw rounds start with the player to the left of the player who started the previous draw round.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for this draw poker variant with special draw rules.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Suits are not ranked in hand comparison; standard poker hand rankings apply. All four suits are equal for determining the high hand.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit in standard poker order: ace high, then king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two. Standard hand rankings from high card up to royal flush apply.
engine.dealPattern: Ante, deal five face-down cards each, then repeated draw/bet cycles.

hero.title: ALL FOR ONE
hero.subtitle: The Musketeer Draw
hero.tagline: Exchange one or exchange all. There is no middle ground.

synthesis.shortDescription: A thrilling high-attrition Poker variant. Burn through the deck as you repeatedly swap either one card or your entire hand in a race for the perfect showdown.

prompts.human: Welcome to All for One. You start with 5 cards. In each draw round you may exchange all five, exchange one, or stand pat. Every draw round is followed by betting, and once the stock gets too short for another draw cycle the game goes to showdown.
prompts.ai: Game: All for One and One for All Poker. Flow: ante, deal five down, opening bet, repeated draw+bet loops, showdown. Draw choices are exactly 0, 1, or 5; enforce stock-safety rule on 5-card exchanges.

scoring.description: Pot game scored by standard high-hand poker ranking at showdown.

penalties.Illegal Draw Declaration: A declared 5-card exchange that violates stock-safety must be rejected and replaced by legal choice (1 or stand pat).

scoring.splitRules: Standard poker pot splitting for identical hands.

nullReasons.targetScore: Pot game; each hand resolves independently; no fixed target score.
nullReasons.cardValues: Poker scoring uses standard hand rankings; there is no separate per-card value table for this game.
